speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; could you tell me if these symptoms appeared suddenly or developed gradually over time? Also, do you notice any trouble with swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest, combined with double vision on looking up or down, is very suggestive of myasthenia gravis. To confirm this, I need to know if you have noticed any difficulty swallowing, chewing, or holding your eyelids open. Additionally, are there any other conditions like thyroid issues or recent infections? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies AND MuSK_antibodies.
